headline: The Electrician Foundation
threshold: By Lesson 10, you can greet people on the job, use numbers, time and measurements, describe tools and conditions, ask questions, make polite requests and ask for help in Spanish, and start Electrician Lesson 1.

lessons.title: Sounds and Greetings
lessons.objective: Say job words with clear Spanish sounds and greet coworkers and customers on an electrical job.
lessons.focus: The five vowels, ch, j, ll, rr and the written accent in job words; greetings

words.note: Spanish a is always 'ah'; keep every vowel short and clear.
ch sounds like English 'ch' in 'church'.
j sounds like a strong English h: CA-ha.
ll sounds like y in 'yes'. It also means key.
ll again: tor-NEE-yo.
h is silent; rr is a rolled, trilled r.
The written accent marks the stressed syllable: SÓ-ta-no.
Mexican and US Spanish word for light bulb.
Same word for a woman: la electricista.
Same word for a woman: la ayudante.

words.en: Good morning, my name is Carlos.

words.note: Say it when you meet someone for the first time.
Spanish drops the word for 'a' before a job: literally 'I am electrician'.
Use this greeting from noon until dark.

words.en: How do you say this in Spanish?

lessons.speaking: Greet a coworker, say your name and that you are an electrician, and ask how to say a tool in Spanish.

lessons.title: Numbers, Time and Measurements
lessons.objective: Count to 1,000, tell the start time, and give lengths in feet and inches for wire and materials.
lessons.focus: Numbers 0 to 1,000, clock time, and feet, inches, rolls and packs on the job

words.note: The plural is pies: 10 pies means 10 feet.
Use 'es la' for 1 o'clock and 'son las' for all other hours.
Add 'y media' for half past and 'y cuarto' for quarter past.

lessons.speaking: Tell your helper what time you arrive, how many feet are on a roll of wire, and how many packs of screws you have.

lessons.title: Ser and Estar
lessons.objective: Say what things are and describe their condition or location, like a live wire or a loose screw.
lessons.focus: ser for what something is, estar for its condition or location, like a live wire

words.note: The ending matches the noun: use the -a ending with a feminine word.
For a live wire say energizado or con corriente, not prendido.
For a woman: la dueña.
estar: a condition that can change. Always test before you touch.
ser: what something is like.

words.en: The owner is in the kitchen.
words.es: El dueño está en la cocina.
words.note: estar for location.

lessons.speaking: Tell a coworker whether the wire is live or off, whether a screw is loose, and where the owner is.

lessons.title: Have, There Is, Need and Want
lessons.objective: Say what tools you have, need and want, what is in the truck, and what you have to do safely.
lessons.focus: tener, hay, necesitar, querer and hay que + infinitive for tools and safety steps

words.note: Mexican word; you will also hear destornillador.
Many crews also just say the tester.
Informal form, used between coworkers.

words.en: There's a ladder in the truck.
words.es: Hay una escalera en la troca.
words.note: troca is the common US Spanish word for pickup truck.

words.en: I want to start in the kitchen.
You have to wear safety glasses.
words.es: Hay que usar lentes de seguridad.

words.en: You have to test the wire before touching it.
words.es: Hay que probar el cable antes de tocarlo.
words.note: hay que + infinitive: something everyone must do.

lessons.speaking: Ask a coworker for the tools you need, say what is in the truck, and say what you have to do before touching a wire.

lessons.title: Go, Do and Can
lessons.objective: Say where you are going, what you are going to do, and what you can do in the customer's house.
lessons.focus: ir, ir a + infinitive for plans, hacer and poder around the house and the truck

words.note: Common Mexican word; you will also hear garaje.
Inside it is the ceiling; outside it is the roof.
Mexican word for bedroom.
On the job, often the electrical supply store.

words.en: I'm going to change the bathroom light bulb.
words.es: Voy a cambiar el foco del baño.
words.note: ir a + infinitive talks about plans.

words.en: Tomorrow we do the work in the garage.
words.es: Mañana hacemos el trabajo de la cochera.

words.en: Can I go into the attic?
words.note: The words a and el join to make al.

words.en: We're going to the store at 10.
words.es: Vamos a la tienda a las 10.

lessons.speaking: Tell the homeowner where you are going, what you are going to do today, and ask if you can go into the attic.

lessons.title: Present Tense
lessons.objective: Describe everyday work tasks in the present tense for yourself, a coworker, a customer and the crew.
lessons.focus: Present tense -ar, -er, -ir verbs for yo, tú, usted, nosotros and ellos

words.note: Mexican and US word; you will also hear enchufe.
Mexican word; you will also hear interruptor.
Same word for a woman: la aprendiz.
For a woman: la clienta.

words.en: We work at the customer's house.
words.es: Trabajamos en la casa de la clienta.

words.en: I check the plan and you cut the wire.
words.es: Yo reviso el plano y tú cortas el cable.
words.note: Regular -ar verbs: the I form ends in -o, the informal you form in -as.
Polite form for a customer; this is a regular -ir verb.
Regular -er verb: the he or she form ends in -e.

lessons.speaking: Tell your helper who does what today: you check the plan, they cut the wire, and the crew installs the fan.

lessons.title: Questions
lessons.objective: Ask basic questions about where things are, who is in charge, when you start and how long a wire is.
lessons.focus: Question words qué, quién, dónde, cuándo, cuánto, cómo, por qué, cuál

words.note: Question words always carry a written accent.
It changes to match the noun: -os for masculine plural, -as for feminine plural.
Two words in a question; written as one word it means because.
Use it to ask for names, addresses and choices.
For a woman: la jefa.

words.en: What's the address of the house?
words.es: ¿Cuál es la dirección de la casa?

lessons.speaking: Ask a new coworker where the pliers are, who the boss is, when you start and what the address of the house is.

lessons.title: No, Never and How Much
lessons.objective: Say no, never, nobody, nothing and not yet, and ask for more, less or another on the job.
lessons.focus: no, nunca, nadie, nada, todavía no, más, menos and otro

words.note: Put it before the verb, and you don't need another negative word.
Alone before the verb; if it comes after the verb, also put no before the verb.
When it comes after the verb, also put no before the verb.
Never put the word for 'a' in front of it; it already means another.
Ends in -a but is masculine.
For a woman: la inspectora.

words.en: I need another roll of wire.
I can't see anything without the flashlight.
words.es: No veo nada sin la linterna.

lessons.speaking: Tell the crew lead that the inspector hasn't arrived yet, nobody is in the attic, and you need another roll of wire.

lessons.title: Polite Requests and Commands
lessons.objective: Politely ask a homeowner or coworker to do something and give simple, safe instructions.
lessons.focus: ¿Puede…? requests and usted commands, plus ustedes commands to a crew

words.note: Say it to pass by someone or to enter a room.

words.en: Can you move the car out of the garage?
words.es: ¿Puede sacar el carro de la cochera?
words.note: Can you + infinitive: a polite request to one person.

words.en: Can you open the basement door?

words.note: Polite command to one person; the ending -me means 'to me'.

words.es: No toque los cables, por favor.
words.note: Negative polite command to one person.
Plural command, for the whole crew.

lessons.speaking: Politely ask the homeowner to open the door, move the car and not touch the wires, then ask your crew to bring the ladder.

lessons.title: Words You Already Know and Getting Help
lessons.objective: Recognize Spanish words you already know and ask for help when you don't understand.
lessons.focus: Cognates ending in -ción, -dad, -ente and survival phrases for getting help

words.note: Words ending in -ción are like English -tion and are feminine.
Words ending in -dad are like English -ty and are feminine.
A wire with current is live, the same as energized.
Polite form, for someone you don't know well.

words.en: There's a problem with the connection.
words.es: Hay un problema con la conexión.

lessons.speaking: Tell a coworker you don't understand, ask them to speak more slowly, and say there is a problem and you need help.
